title: Sentry Saddle — night shift runbook (draft)
body:
Purpose / quick context:
This is my personal scratchpad for the night shift (Sentry Saddle). Lightweight, intentionally rough — meant to be read/edited live during handoff. Keep notes to yourself here and add small snippets to Confluence or the final runbook after the shift.

Shift summary (start):
- State: most services green; occasional 5xx spikes on hosted-api-prod-us-east-1 route between 02:10–02:25 — suspected transient GPU node OOMs.
- Open/persistent alerts: api-5xx-rate (firing), kv-cache-hit-drop (warning).
- Anything on-going I haven't closed: see "Active items" below.

Active items (actionable):
1) api-5xx-rate (medium) — alert group: production/hosted-api
   - Symptom: burst of 500s clustered on /v1/generate, 95th latency spike, traces show model-worker restarts.
   - Quick diagnostics:
     - kubectl get pods -n hosted-prod | grep model-worker  # check restarts
     - kubectl logs <pod> -n hosted-prod --since=10m | egrep "OOM|Killed|traceback"
     - datadog: "trace.search(service:hosted-api AND http.status_code:500)" (last 30m)
   - Temporary mitigation: route traffic to dedicated-fallback pool: update feature-flag -> routing.fallback=dedicated-v2 (see ops-flag playbook) OR bump capacity via autoscale-burst (15m).
   - Notes: last night Diego forced a rolling reboot on three g4dn nodes; probably same host pool flaky. If node restarts >2x, page infra oncall (Samir).

2) kv-cache-hit-drop (low)
   - Symptom: L1 cache hit rate dropped from 84% -> 62% for embeddings route (spike at 01:40).
   - Quick checks: redis-prod-cluster health, RPS, eviction count.
     - redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 info stats | grep evicted_keys
     - grafana dashboard: infra/redis-cache -> eviction rate, used_memory_peak
   - Temporary mitigation: clear hot-prefixes (manual prefix eviction) only if eviction_count growing AND we see tail latency regress. Avoid full flush.

Important commands cheat-sheet (copy these to terminal when handing off):
- kubectl top nodes
- kubectl get pods -n hosted-prod -o wide | sort -k6
- kubectl logs -n hosted-prod <pod> --since=15m | tail -n 200
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="tags:hosted-prod" --zones=us-east1-b
- prometheus query (PromQL): rate(http_requests_total{job="hosted-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])
- redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 slowlog get 50

Dashboards/links (quick):
- Datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/hosted-api-overview
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ops/redis-cache
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.local/trace-search?service=hosted-api
- Infra incidents: Confluence doc: /confluence/display/OPS/infra-incidents (copy summary after shift)

Escalation & contacts (fast):
- Night pager (primary): Samir Kapoor — pager: +1-555-0134, slack: @samir
- Infra lead (on-call backup): Diego Rivera — slack: @diego (do not page unless >2 node failures)
- Platform eng (weekdays only): Nina Patel — slack: @nina
- On-call rotation notes: check #ops-oncall in Slack for current overrides

Handoff checklist (what I will tell next person):
- Topline: "api-5xx-rate is firing; I traced to model-worker restarts on hosted-prod pool; I routed traffic to dedicated-fallback and opened INF-4232 for follow-up. kv-cache hit % low — watching redis evictions. No other user-facing degradation."
- Steps already done: scaled fallback, checked node restarts, collected logs to /tmp/ava-night-0305.tgz
- Files/artifacts I created: logs tarball (GCS): gs://redwood-ops/night-logs/ava-20260305.tar.gz; created JIRA INF-4232 with traces attached
- Anything I would do next: if 500s come back, trigger immediate fallback to regional-dedicated and page Samir; if kv eviction continues for >30m, consider hot-prefix purge with Diego

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Investigate whether the autoscaler observed noisy signals leading to node churn; check controller logs (/var/log/kube-controller-manager).
- Remember to copy the "request shape" sample for INF-4232 to the eval harness so product can reproduce latency.
- Is the recent quantized model config (q8b) causing larger memory footprint than expected? Cross-check model config PR (linked artifact).

Playbook snippets (keep short):
- Rolling restart of model-worker on a node (safe sequence):
  1) cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
  2) drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
  3) restart container runtime / VM reboot if needed
  4) uncordon after stable: kubectl uncordon <node>
  Note: prefer restarting single node at a time; rolling all nodes at once breaks cache warmup.

Common quick triage questions (answer before escalating):
- Is the issue global or regional? check latency/5xx per region in datadog
- Are worker restarts correlated with specific model variants? filter traces by model_id
- Are there recent infra deploys or PRs landing in last 30–60min? check github PRs and CI deploy history

Unresolved / To follow up after shift:
- INF-4232: attach sample trace + request shape + memory metrics
- Confirm autoscaler anomaly at 02:05 — assign to Diego for post-mortem
- Add a small runbook step to routing service to automate temporary fallback for this class of 5xx (product + infra review required)

Random scratch / thoughts (notes-to-self language allowed):
- If I get woken up by a 5xx ping at 03:00, scream internally but apply graceful fallback first.
- Can't forget to ack the Slack thread and leave a brief summary before closing INF-4232.

End of shift quick message to include for handoff: 
"Heads up — api-5xx-rate firing; routed to fallback pool; collecting logs (gs://redwood-ops/night-logs/ava-20260305.tar.gz). Watching redis evictions. No full-prod impact yet but please monitor traces for repeating restarts. Tag me if it escalates. — Ava"

Last edited: 2026-03-05 by Ava (this doc is draft/scratch; will tidy later).
